quote: I don't know. I just bought the house.
stewart_read: Customer has no bill history as a brand-new owner; this is a legitimate data gap, not resistance, and the rep needs a clean pivot.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as an objection to giving financial info, but the follow-up context (talks about previous owner's data) confirms it's a genuine gap.
coaching_implication: Rep should immediately offer the 'use current app/kWh reading' path instead of first explaining why the bill is needed.

quote: I can tell you what my kilowatt usage is right now.
stewart_read: Customer proactively offers usage data as a workaround, essentially building the bridge for the rep, but the rep doesn't reflect it back as leverage before moving to the photo-text ask.
coaching_implication: Rep could acknowledge this offer explicitly ('perfect, that's exactly what we need') to reinforce the customer's cooperative energy before pivoting.

quote: Yeah. As of right now, it's a 182
stewart_read: The bill/usage figure is captured but never flipped into an emotional reason to act against the utility — it's filed and the call moves to roof type.
coaching_implication: Missed opportunity to tie the number to a savings-oriented reframe per coaching_philosophy.bill_anchoring.

quote: So you just got it. Let me tell him you just got it the house, like, last month, this last two months.
stewart_read: Rep pauses the call to go consult someone about the new-homeowner, no-bill-history situation before confirming the appointment can proceed.
coaching_implication: This scenario (brand-new homeowner, no bill) should have a standard playbook answer so setters don't need a live hold.

quote: it has to be on the rear of the house. It cannot be, seen from the street.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a specific placement preference near the very end, showing genuine forward planning and investment in the install, not just going through motions.
coaching_implication: Rep handled this fine by deferring to the specialist, but could have briefly noted it as a good sign of engagement rather than a purely logistical aside.

quote: K. So I got you twenty seventh at noon.
stewart_read: Appointment time is set but the rep skips the hour-block, no-driving/computer instruction, and explicit 'is that fair?' handshake before hanging up.
coaching_implication: Button-up should be run in full even on an easy, cooperative call — missing elements raise no-show risk regardless of customer warmth.
